paper_title: Novel cosmological bounds on thermally-produced axion-like particles
notes: Headline result: 95% CL upper bounds on the axion-gluon coupling Cg/fa (Cg=1 corresponds to 1/f_a) from Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE + BAO, presented in Fig. 8 (blue diamonds, bounding the shaded excluded region) at the nine fixed masses ma = {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,0.1,1,3,10,30,100} eV of the LCDM+DeltaNeff runs (Sec. 5.2). Points extracted by pixel analysis of the raster figure Constraints_Cg_gd.pdf from the e-print, axes calibrated on the tick marks. Cross-checks: marginalised bound Cg/fa < 1.06e-7 GeV^-1 (Planck+BAO, Table 2/Eq. 5.2) matches the low-mass points; the Planck+ACT+BAO comparison in Sec. 5.2 implies the Planck+BAO bound at ma=1e-4 eV is ~1.59e-7 GeV^-1, vs 1.50e-7 extracted. The paper stresses cosmology directly constrains Cg/fa, while the equivalent EDM coupling (right axis of Fig. 8) follows the model-dependent Eq. (2.4): gd [GeV^-2] = 3.54e-3 GeV^-1 x (Cg/fa) (ratio from Table 2, e.g. gd<3.77e-10 GeV^-2 for Cg/fa<1.06e-7 GeV^-1). Alternative scenario not reported: Planck-alone (orange) curve, slightly stronger for ma<~0.1 eV. The paper also bounds g_agamma (Fig. 7), but presents the gluon bound as its main result (strongest to date, superseding SN1987A). Not a dark-matter-density-dependent limit (thermal relic abundance), so no rho_DM rescaling.
